memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle." - Exod 40:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the moment the whole book has been travelling toward.

Exodus began with slaves crying out in Egypt. It ends with God's glory settling among them. Everything in between — the plagues, the sea, the mountain, the calf, the building — leads here.

And notice what God says by doing this. He had said in chapter 33 that He would not go with them. Moses pleaded. And now the glory does not merely accompany them; it fills the tent at the centre of their camp.

Grace had the last word.

Even Moses could not enter. The glory was too much, too full, too holy. That tells us this was no mere symbol — God genuinely came.

But hold onto the trajectory. The glory that filled a tent later filled a temple (1 Kgs 8:11), then took human form — the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory (John 1:14). The word John uses means "tabernacled."

And now, astonishingly, God's Spirit dwells in His people. Do you not know that you yourselves are God's temple? (1 Cor 3:16).

The glory that Moses could not enter now lives in ordinary believers, because Christ made a way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does it amaze you that God chooses to dwell with people?
2. How does it change your day to know God's Spirit lives in you?
3. What has God brought you through this year that ends in His presence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You came down to dwell among Your people, and now You dwell in me. I can hardly take it in. Thank You. Amen.
